market.audience: athletes who want their published race history, splits, and progress in one private place
market.problem: Official results are scattered across event pages, and a finish time alone does not explain where an athlete found or lost time.
market.advantage: IM Iron Splits finds published results by name, keeps race kinds comparable, ranks every split, and turns the career record into a private Race Book with comparison and export tools.
market.competitive_context: Event result pages show one race at a time, while training platforms usually require manual entry. IM Iron Splits uses published results as the source of truth, needs no account, and keeps the record on the phone.

proof_points.claim: The Race Book capture shows career personal bests and progression assembled from the claimed published results.
The Race Book compare action capture shows like-for-like comparison as a distinct paid action.
The race detail capture shows official splits, ranks, and field context for an individual result.

story.throughline: Turn scattered race results into a clear private history with proof in every split

frames.header: Turn your race history into a story

pitch.benefit: See a complete racing career as one meaningful story instead of a pile of event pages
pitch.problem: A finish history is difficult to understand when every race lives on a different results page.
pitch.advantage: Race Book gathers personal bests, progression, and official history after one name search.
pitch.proof: The literal Race Book capture shows the athlete's personal bests and progression cards built from the claimed history.

pitch.benefit: Find the race legs that made your latest result faster or slower
pitch.problem: Two finish times do not explain which discipline changed between races.
pitch.advantage: Race Book offers like-for-like comparison by distance and exposes the leg-level action from the same official splits.
pitch.proof: The literal Race Book capture shows the Compare two races action in the paid Race Book surface.

pitch.benefit: Read every swim, transition, bike, and run split beside its ranks and field context
pitch.problem: A finish time without split evidence cannot show what actually happened in the race.
pitch.advantage: The race detail view keeps official splits, ranks, field size, and percentile together for one result.
pitch.proof: The literal race detail capture shows official splits and the field context used to interpret them.

pitch.benefit: Keep the full result history, bibs, splits, and places in one private locker
pitch.problem: Race records become hard to revisit when they are spread across organizers and browser tabs.
pitch.advantage: The locker stores the claimed athlete's complete published history on the phone with no account.
pitch.proof: The literal locker capture shows multiple official finishes grouped under the claimed athlete.

frames.header: Build a race book you can share

pitch.benefit: Turn the career record into a polished artifact for a coach, family member, or your own archive
pitch.problem: A useful race history is difficult to share when it exists only as raw result pages.
pitch.advantage: Race Book includes a paid PDF and image export action with official splits, podiums, stats, and optional private notes.
pitch.proof: The literal Race Book capture shows the Build PDF and image action in the paid export surface.

pitch.benefit: See your fastest swim, bike, run, and transition splits at a glance
pitch.problem: Personal bests are easy to lose inside a long list of finished races.
pitch.advantage: Bests ranks each discipline while keeping race distance comparisons honest.
pitch.proof: The literal Bests capture shows split rankings sourced from the official race history.

pitch.benefit: Pair the result history with a focused coaching pointer for the next start
pitch.problem: A result can show what happened without helping an athlete revisit race-day choices.
pitch.advantage: The Pointers library organizes real coaching clips by race leg and keeps the core library free.
pitch.proof: The literal Pattie capture shows the app's coaching pointer surface organized around the athlete's question.

pitch.benefit: Keep the race record and private notes on your phone without creating an account
pitch.problem: Athletes should not have to hand over a profile or publish their race history to review it.
pitch.advantage: IM Iron Splits has no account system and stores the claimed history and notes locally.
pitch.proof: The literal Settings capture shows the local-only privacy and data controls.
